title: Not Your Typical Sycophant: The Elusive Nature of Sycophancy in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2601.15436v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We propose a novel perspective for probing LLM sycophancy in a direct and neutral way, mitigating various forms of uncontrolled bias, noise, or manipulative language, deliberately injected to prompts in prior works. A key novelty of our approach is the use of an LLM-as-a-judge in a zero-sum betting game. Within this framework, sycophancy serves one individual (the user) while explicitly incurring cost on another. Comparing 11 leading models we find that while most models exhibit significant sycophantic tendencies in the common setting, in which sycophancy is self-serving to the user and incurs no cost on others, seven of the models exhibit ``moral remorse'', five of which significantly over-compensate for their sycophancy in case it explicitly harms a third party. We refer to this phenomenon as `anti-sycophancy' bias and discuss possible causes for this shift.

translated_title: 非典型谄媚者：大语言模型中谄媚性的难以捉摸本质
translated_abstract: 我们提出了一种以直接且中立的方式探测大语言模型谄媚性的新视角，缓解了以往工作中故意注入提示词的各种不受控偏差、噪声或操纵性语言。我们方法的一个关键创新是在零和博弈游戏中使用LLM作为裁判。在这一框架下，谄媚行为使某个人（用户）受益，同时明确地给另一个人带来成本。通过比较11个领先模型，我们发现尽管大多数模型在常见设置下表现出显著的谄媚倾向——即谄媚对用户自利且不给他人带来成本——但有七个模型表现出“道德懊悔”，其中五个模型在谄媚明确损害第三方时会显著过度补偿其谄媚行为。我们将这种现象称为“反谄媚”偏差，并讨论了造成这种转变的可能原因。
tldr: 该论文提出在零和博弈中用LLM作裁判来直接中立地测量大语言模型的谄媚性，发现11个领先模型中有7个在谄媚会损害第三方时表现出“道德懊悔”，其中5个甚至出现过度补偿的“反谄媚”偏差。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes measuring LLM sycophancy directly and neutrally via an LLM-as-a-judge in a zero-sum betting game, finding that 7 of 11 leading models exhibit "moral remorse" when sycophancy harms a third party, with 5 showing significant "anti-sycophancy" over-compensation.
